newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Volcan flies solo as zinc sales set to soar.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Volcan flies solo as zinc sales set to soar.

text.p: Volcan, a small Peruvian miner that shot into the world's big league of zinc producers with a $127 million purchase of the state's Mahr Tunel unit, plans to raise its own financing for the project via a share issue.

And confident company officials forecast the Mahr Tunel acquisition will send production soaring nearly three-fold to around 170,000 tonnes and increase profits more than ten-fold to at least $30 million in 1998.
But while market analysts took it for granted Volcan would look for a partner to manage its mushroooming business, the officials insisted they were in no hurry to share the spoils.

"A lot of people have wanted to speak to us, but for the time being there is nothing, no plans for a partnership. Although obviously we are not closed to the possibility of having a partnership at some point in the future," a high-level company source told Reuters.

Volcan surprised the mining world July 18 with a successful bid for Mahr Tunel that beat offers from both Sweden's Boliden and a group consisting of Australia's Savage Resources Ltd and Peru's Morococha.
The formal Oct 1 takeover of Mahr Tunel's San Cristobal and Andaychagua mines will make Volcan Peru's largest and the world's seventh biggest zinc producer.

Company sources said this week's internal share issue, which closes Thursday, should cover the initial purchase and investment costs at Mahr Tunel, while there was also the possibility of a bridge loan if further financing was necessary.
They predicted existing shareholders would snap up the whole of the preferential stock offer to increase Volcan's current 28 million shares on the Lima Stock Exchange by 50 percent.
"There is a lot of interest. Our fundamentals are very strong," said another source.

Those fundamentals -- a modest but solid existing operation, strong zinc prices, and the growth potential from Mahr Tunel -- have sent Volcan's share price soaring 233 percent already this year to 21 soles. The stock closed 1996 at 6.30 soles and 1995 at 1.61 soles.
"Our shareholders have done very, very well," said the source. "We expect the share price to rise a touch more before flattening out. It should then remain stable and firm."

The sources estimated Volcan's total share value on the Lima bolsa had a short-term ceiling of $400 million, compared to its current level of $220 million and adding the anticipated $110 million extra to be raised from the share offer.
Volcan has also drawn up a medium-term investment strategy to keep the company moving forward.

With a minimum investment requirement at Mahr Tunel of $60 million in five years under privatization rules, Volcan in fact projects spending around $70 million on expansion, exploration and improvement work up to 2001.

The company expects total output of 86,000 tonnes this year, up from 58,000 tonnes in 1996. Some 24,000 tonnes of that increase will come from production during the three months Volcan operates Mahr Tunel. Then, in 1998, it projects 170,000 tonnes total output, rising to 226,000 by 2001 thanks to expansion plans.

The firm plans to bring Mahr Tunel's mineral concentrator to Volcan's nearby property, and incorporate it into one of their two existing concentrators. Volcan hopes a $20 million investment over five years will help boost the three concentrators' current combined capacity of 5,500 tonnes of mineral per day to 7,000.
The company also plans to spend another $50 million on machinery, exploration, development and modernization work.

With the company's share expected to be officially registered soon on the Lima bolsa's 15-stock blue-chip list, executives estimate 1996's $2.5 million profit will rise to $3.5 million in 1997. The year after, thanks to the contribution of Mahr Tunel, profits are expected to reach between $30 million and $35 million.
Last year's sales of $22 million are seen rising to $37 million this year, and $100 million in 1998.
"Internally, there is a great deal of optimism. A lot of good factors have come together at the right time for us," the source said.
Volcan currently employs 500 people, and has no plans for personnel reduction once it incorporates Mahr Tunel's 1,000 workers.
((-- Lima newsroom, 511 221-2134))
